The Dallas Cowboys have the unenviable task of trying to contain the high-flying attack of Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers in this coming Sunday’s Week 10 showdown at AT&T Stadium in Arlington. Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker surely is looking at ways to slow down San Francisco’s offense, and one that he is particularly concerned about is the Niners’ pre-snap activities , as pointed out by Ed Werder of WFAA. “Cowboys DC Christian Parker, when asked about the 49ers using presnap motion at the highest rate in the league, stressed the importance of eye discipline and to know where opponents are when ball actually snapped because ‘You don’t want to be chasing that rabbitt all day,’” Werder shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter. They are also putting up 376.8 total yards per outing, and that’s despite dealing with numerous injuries. Brock Purdy has been as steady as they come at quarterback, coming into this showdown versus the Cowboys with a league-best 81.4 quarterback rating. With weapons like do-it-all running back Christian McCaffrey and star tight end George Kittle, the 49ers have been quite a lot to deal. The 49ers love to find mismatches, and those pre-snap movements are key to making that happen for them. It is going to be a big challenge for Parker to devise an effective plan against that San Francisco offense . On the season, the Cowboys are just 25th in the league with 26.2 points allowed per game and 30th with 372.7 total yards given up per outing. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. The Blazers open the 2026-27 NBA season Wednesday night against the Phoenix Suns — a team they upset in April in the play-in tournament — and if you’re just now tuning in for the start of the regular season, well, there’s a lot you missed. The backcourt duo is joining a fivesome that includes returning starters Deni Avdija , Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan . It’s a versatile, star-studded lineup that features three All-Stars, a former All-Defensive Second Team selection, one of the best young centers in the NBA and loads of scoring potential. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.description: Image Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Chargers’ biggest mistake at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline after Daiyan Henley trade fell through appeared first on ClutchPoints . They sent linebacker Daiyan Henley to Denver but held their best remaining trade chip on a winless team. The Henley deal has since collapsed , so Los Angeles ended the deadline with no sale at all. Henley Trade Collapsed Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The Chargers agreed to send Henley to the Broncos for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder shortly before Tuesday’s deadline. Henley had been their leading tackler for three straight seasons, with 142 tackles in 2024, 101 last year and 51 so far in 2026. The agreement was contingent on a physical. Late Wednesday, Denver announced the trade would not be finalized after the Broncos raised concerns about one of Henley’s knees and tried to renegotiate before the sides gave up. Henley stays with the Chargers, and Denver keeps its picks. The Chargers’ only deadline move now looks like a failure. Los Angeles was willing to sell a pending free agent for modest Day 3 picks, which shows it recognized the value of selling. It simply declined to do the same with a better asset. USA Today called him likely the Chargers’ best trade asset. Contenders needed pass rush help, and Chicago was among the teams linked to him. The Athletic noted a possible Day 3 return. A pick like that is not franchise-changing, but it is more than the Chargers will get by letting him leave in free agency. item.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong's 'quantum leap' landed an unlikely MVP campaign
item.description: Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong outdueled Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani for the NL MVP award. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS A player's development is rarely linear in baseball. After taking several steps forward, it's not unusual to see someone move one or two steps backward. Coming into the 2026 season, the Chicago Cubs were waiting to see which direction Pete Crow-Armstrong headed. Nearly nine months later, the superstar center fielder showed the baseball world that his struggles were minor hurdles en route to becoming one of the best players in the sport. Crow-Armstrong was named National League MVP on Thursday night , making him the youngest player to win the award (24) since Cody Bellinger (23) won the NL MVP in 2019. PCA received all 30 first-place votes , beating four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani, who had won the award in 2024 and '25, and Milwaukee Brewers star Brice Turang. "I want to be better than I was the day before and really that's been all that I've needed to motivate myself with for as long as I can remember," PCA said on the MLB Network broadcast after winning the award. "I've had really important people that wake me up every day." Being named the 2026 NL MVP is the cherry on top in a season full of deserved accolades for Crow-Armstrong. What made this season, in which he became the seventh player in MLB history to join the 40-40 club, even more special was that his dominance shined with his bat and glove. Crow-Armstrong won his second Gold Glove Award and was honored with the NL's Platinum Glove Award winner as the best defender in the league. What makes PCA's 2026 season so remarkable is the turnaround it took to make it happen. Crow-Armstrong's second half in '25 in which he carried a .634 OPS was one to forget, but the 2026 NL MVP knew he had to come into the season with a new offensive plan. And after signing a six-year, $116 million deal right before the season began, the pressure was on to show he could be the star the Cubs hoped he would be. The first six weeks of the season, it looked like the player who ended 2025 had returned and it would be more of the same. But Crow-Armstrong quickly showed he was not only a different player, but the NL's best player. From May 1 until the end of the regular season, he became must-see TV as his highlight-reel defense in center field, tape-measure homers and electric speed captivated baseball. item.title: Outgoing WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert gives update on search for replacement
item.description: © Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Outgoing WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert gives update on search for replacement appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The WNBA has begun interviewing candidates to replace outgoing commissioner Cathy Engelbert , although a timeline for selecting her successor remains uncertain. Engelbert provided an update on the search Thursday, following the league’s annual competition committee meetings, according to ESPN’s Alexa Philippou. Engelbert described the search as an “ongoing process” and declined to disclose how many candidates are being considered. Asked whether she expects the league to hire its next commissioner by Dec. 31, Engelbert said, “I hope so.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The update comes nearly two months after Engelbert announced in September that she would retire following the 2026 WNBA season, ending a tenure that began in 2019 when she became the first commissioner in league history. Engelbert previously addressed the search ahead of Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Oct. 17, revealing that she had been working toward identifying her successor for three years. According to ESPN’s Kendra Andrews, Engelbert said at the time that the league had hired Excel to oversee the formal search process. Engelbert and others had submitted recommendations for potential candidates, and she indicated there was considerable interest in the position. Thursday’s comments confirm that the process has progressed, although Engelbert did not identify any candidates or provide additional details about when a final decision might be announced. Engelbert, 61, announced her retirement after more than seven years leading the WNBA and more than four decades working in business. “After more than seven years at the WNBA and more than 40 total years in business, I have made the decision to retire as WNBA Commissioner,” Engelbert said in September. Her tenure coincided with substantial growth in the league, including increased television viewership and the introduction of private charter flights for teams. The WNBA also experienced heightened interest surrounding players such as Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese, Paige Bueckers and A’ja Wilson. NBA commissioner Adam Silver praised Engelbert’s leadership following her retirement announcement. “Cathy has presided over the WNBA through the most significant period of growth in the league’s 30-year history,” Silver said. “We are grateful for Cathy’s leadership and unwavering commitment to the advancement of women’s basketball.” Engelbert’s latest comments leave open whether the WNBA will have a new commissioner in place before the end of 2026.

item.title: Sydney Swans players will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
item.description: Isaac Heeney is among the players police say will not be charged over an incident at a hotel in August [Getty] Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said. After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement. Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August. The men previously denied wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking. Australian media reported that three women, understood to be adult entertainers, had alleged inappropriate touching during the incident at the Pullman Hotel and are reportedly looking into civil action. "Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment," police said in a statement on Friday. A fifth player, Riley Bice, who was also suspended by the club, had already been cleared by police. Heeney welcomed the police announcement, saying the past three months had been "incredibly difficult for my family, [my fiancee] Steffie and those close to me". "To my family and friends, your love and loyalty has meant more than words can do justice," he continued.

item.title: Michigan basketball signs Lucai Anderson, lone class of 2027 commit
item.description: Michigan basketball's lone class of 2027 prospect is officially on board. Lucai Anderson, a four-star guard out of IMG Academy in Bradenton, Florida, officially signed with the Wolverines on Thursday, Nov. 12. The younger brother of former Michigan commit Christian Anderson Jr. (who ultimately played at Texas Tech and became a first round NBA Draft pick last summer) is ranked the No. 8 shooting guard in the nation, the No. 17 player in Florida and No. 83 overall prospect in the class of 2027 per 247 Sports' composite rankings. "From the first time I visited Michigan, I felt like it was a place where I could really see myself," Anderson said in a statement. "Coach Boynton and his staff made me feel like family, and I really connected with their vision for the program and the way they want to play. Michigan has an incredible basketball tradition, and I'm excited to be part of it. "I'm ready to get to work, compete for championships and help continue that tradition." The 6-foot-4 playmaker spent his sophomore and junior seasons at Trinity Christian School (Lubbock, Texas) where he scored 1,532 points in 69 games (22.2 points per game) and earned Texas Association of Basketball Coaches (TABC) All-State honors and district Offensive Player of the Year recognition as junior. Anderson played for Germany at the 2026 FIBA U18 EuroBasket in Italy and led the national team in scoring, at 15 points per game, and assists (4.9). He helped Germany finish fifth with a 6-1 record and qualify for the 2027 FIBA U19 World Cup. “Lucai is a really talented young man who has a great feel for the game," Michigan coach Mike Boynton Jr. said in a statement. “He can score, he can make plays for others, and I love that he's comfortable doing both. He's competed at a high level here and overseas, and you can see how those experiences have helped him grow as a player.” Anderson is the lone recruit in the class of 2027, which means the Wolverines will need to go heavy in the transfer portal next year; Roddy Gayle Jr., Kenny Noland and Jalen Reed all out of eligibility after this season. The Wolverines could also lose Trey McKenney, Elliot Cadeau, JP Estrella, Moustapha Thiam, Brandon McCoy Jr. and Quinn Costello to the professional ranks. “What I've enjoyed most is getting to know Lucai and his family," Boynton said. "He's a great young man who wants to get better, wants to be coached and wants to be part of something special. That's exactly the kind of person we want at Michigan, and we're really excited about his future here.” Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. item.description: MILWAUKEE, WI - SEPTEMBER 08: Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong (4) slides into second under the tag of Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang (2) during a game between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Chicago Cubs at American Family Field, on September 8, 2026 in Milwaukee, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images For the first time in four years, Shohei Ohtani will not add an MVP trophy to his collection, and for the first time in six years, neither Ohtani nor Aaron Judge is an MVP. Instead, the Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong and the Astros’ Yordan Alvarez both became first-time MVPs, as both players were unanimously elected. Crow-Armstrong, 24, was easily the best player in baseball by several stats, finishing with 10.6 fWAR and 9.8 bWAR as he hit .280/.372/.570 with a major-league-best 45 homers and 119 runs scored, plus 107 RBIs, 31 doubles, eight triples, and 41 steals. His 45 homers and 41 steals made him the seventh player in MLB history to have a 40-40 season, and only the third to hit 45 homers, swipe 40 bags, and collect 30 doubles in one year, joining Ohtani (2024) and Alfonso Soriano (2006). Defensively, he also earned his second consecutive Gold Glove Award and won the NL’s Platinum Glove for the first time. He posted a +26 fielding run value, setting a Statcast-era record for an outfielder, and his +26 outs above average tied Byron Buxton (2017) for the most by an outfielder. Crow-Armstrong received all 30 first-place votes for the award, while Ohtani received 26 second-place votes, two third-place votes, and two fourth-place votes to finish second overall. The Brewers’ Brice Turang came in third, receiving one third-place vote and plenty of votes for third, fourth, and fifth, while NL Cy Young winner Jacob Misiorowski finished fifth. He also turned things on down the stretch, leading the majors in average (.361) and on-base percentage (.475) in the month of September before leading the World Series-winning Crew with 11 walks across 13 playoff games. Turang becomes the first Brewers infielder to finish in the top three in MVP voting since Prince Fielder finished third back in 2011, the same year Ryan Braun won the award. item.title: Shohei Ohtani lost the MVP to Pete Crow-Armstrong. What he needs to do to reclaim it
item.description: Shohei Ohtani waves while rounding the bases after a three-run home run during the second inning of Game 4 of the NLCS. (Gina Ferazzi / Los Angeles Times) When the Dodgers and Cubs met at the beginning of August, it was notable that Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong was even challenging Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani for National League most valuable player. Ohtani was on a streak of three straight MVP seasons and working to return to the mound after what was expected to be a temporary shutdown around the All-Star break. So even as Ohtani and Crow-Armstrong traded leadoff home runs, it felt like a peak in a race that could tilt in Ohtani’s favor in the final months of the season. Tilt it did — the other way. Read more: Dodgers will be involved in Tarik Skubal's free agency, but will they sign him? Ohtani never did return to the mound, and his offense suffered as injuries mounted down the stretch. Crow-Armstrong never cooled off and ran away with the MVP, officially claiming the award Thursday in a unanimous vote. He was the 11th unanimous NL MVP in the history of the award. Ohtani finished second. Ohtani’s two-way skillset is so unique that any time he pitches and hits for an entire season, he’s practically guaranteed the MVP — he won the award twice with the Angels in 2021 and 2023 before winning two with the Dodgers in 2024 and 2025. But the Dodgers’ first attempt at guiding him though a full two-way season crashed and burned in the wake of a lingering left knee injury and recurring right biceps issue. Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs. (Isaac Wasserman / Getty Images) The Dodgers are set on having Ohtani return to two-way duties in 2027. But now they’re left to diagnose what went wrong this year and figure out how to avoid the same pitfalls moving forward. “The good thing is, it’s going to be a normal offseason,” general manager Brandon Gomes said, referring to Ohtani’s health status. “And as we get deeper into the offseason, understanding what our roster looks like, and then having those conversations of, ‘How do we best lay this out to set everybody up to be as good as they can come October?’ “And that’s always the goal. I know it’s so boring and we pound it into the ground. But I think for Sho in particular, it’s like, ‘Hey, let’s get back to feeling 100%, have the normal offseason, like you’re going to have, and then have that conversation based on what our team looks like and rotation and all of that.” The Dodgers have made clear that plotting Ohtani’s pitching plan will be a collaborative effort that will involve conversations throughout the year. item.title: 4 OU players to watch this week against Ole Miss
item.description: The Oklahoma Sooners will see a lot of the Ole Miss Rebels over the next few years in the SEC, as the league has deemed the two teams annual rivals for the next four seasons, starting this year. Combine that with the Sooners and the Rebels already facing off in OU's first two SEC seasons, and the two programs with virtually no shared history are going to get very familiar with each other. Oklahoma is 0-3 against Ole Miss, and the next chance to win comes this week, as the Sooners return home to Norman. OU got a cathartic road win over Florida last week, while Ole Miss was dominated at home by Georgia last week. Two teams with very different mindsets will meet on Owen Field on Saturday afternoon. After the unexpected victory, the Sooners will lean on some key players to try to win two games in a row for the first time since November of 2025. As always with OU, injury concerns will force certain players to step up and help the program make a bowl game with a win this week. Here are four players to watch for the Sooners against the Rebels. 1. Rocky Beers, TE With interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten at the controls, several pass-catchers saw an expanded role in OU's victory in "The Swamp." That included the tight ends, where Rocky Beers leads the way. With his position coach and one of the greatest TEs ever to play dialing up the offense, it's safe to assume Beers will be targeted a lot against the Rebels. OU's passing game options are as healthy right now as they've been all season. Beers has been an important part of the passing attack all season long, and he's somebody that is clearly trusted to get open and make important catches at important moments. In a game where the offense will have to produce more than it did last week, Beers could play a huge role. 2. Lloyd Avant, RB Oklahoma made more of a commitment to the running game against Florida, shortening the game by bleeding the clock and keeping the ball on the ground and out of harm's way. As well as it worked against the Gators, it's hard to see Witten going away from it to start this game. With fellow running back Tory Blaylock's status up in the air for Saturday, it could mean an increased workload for OU's top RB, Lloyd Avant. The Sooners seem to have settled on a starting offensive line of Michael Fasusi, Noah Best, Jake Maikkula, Heath Ozaeta, and E'Marion Harris, and that group being healthy and working together is good news for any OU ball carrier. Avant continues to get the most opportunities of any Sooner running back, and if Blaylock can't play, he could get more totes or still split carries with Jonathan Hatton Jr. 3. item.description: SAN DIEGO, CA - JUNE 09: Will Wagner #7 of the San Diego Padres bats during the game between the Cincinnati Reds and the San Diego Padres at Petco Park on Tuesday, June 9, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Ryan Levy/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Will Wagner The son of Hall-of-Famer Billy Wagner, Will Wagner was drafted by the Houston Astros in 2021 as a passable infielder with solid offensive marks. He’s been solid throughout his minor-league career, with a .287/.390/.429 slash line. Wagner came to the Padres in an under-the-radar deal with the Toronto Blue Jays at the 2025 Trade Deadline. He’s produced modest results despite his lack of time at the big-league level. Overall Grade: B- Wagner started off the season on the injured list with an oblique strain that he suffered in early March. That caused him to play in just 86 games between the minors and majors. Sixteen of those came with the big-league club. Wagner joined the Padres in June, slashing .257/.422/.286 (35 at-bats). The on-base percentage is the shocking number in that grouping. Wagner walked 10 times with nine hits in 45 plate appearances, resulting in him reaching base at a .422 clip. His stats in the minors followed a similar trend, with a .254/.368/.377 slash line in 70 minor-league games. item.title: ‘How’s your mom doing?’: Josh Hokit takes aim at Ciryl Gane, flips off Alex Pereira ahead of UFC 334
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 12: Josh Hokit is seen on stage during the UFC 334 press conference at Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden on November 12, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Josh Hokit may not be everybody’s favorite but he certainly had the crowd on his side at the UFC 334 pre-fight press conference. Wearing goggles, a pad on his neck and a protective cup, Hokit ratcheted up his trash talk with a very receptive New York crowd behind him. While he’s the challenger heading into the title fight, Hokit enjoyed a raucous crowd living and breathing on his every word including when he asked them to get behind him in ai chant against Gane. “I want you to yell at the top of your lungs ‘F*ck Ciryl Gane’ on three!” Hokit shouted to the crowd. “Hey Ciryl, how’s your mom doing? Get on Facetime, I don’t give a f*ck. You know what I’m saying? “This is the champion? Get the f*ck out of here bitch.” Hokit also send a rather loud message to the rest of the heavyweight division and anybody complaining about him getting a title shot after only four wins in the UFC. “F*ck the division,” Hokit shouted. “F*ck Ciryl Gane. It’s the end of this man’s career. Ciryl Gane, say goodbye to your career.” While UFC CEO Dana White admitted that he wasn’t a fan of Hokit’s “schtick,” he defended him getting the title shot on Saturday. For his part, Hokit didn’t seem bothered that White wasn’t a fan of his antics and said ultimately his boss really just cares about exciting fights and that’s what he provides. “All the shenanigans aside, I’m the one in this division putting on good fights,” Hokit said. While the vast majority of his energy was aimed at trash talking Gane, Hokit even took a moment to react to former UFC light heavyweight and middleweight champion Alex Pereira taking a seat in the front row during the press conference. Hokit spent weeks blasting Pereira and potentially setting up a future fight between them before he was granted his title shot at UFC 334. As soon as he saw the Brazilian sit down, Hokit stood up and stuck his middle finger in the air before addressing Pereira directly. “I’m going to chama on his mama,” Hokit said. “He ain’t going to do shit about it. F*ck you.”

item.description: So, y’all wanna win a Big East title? When the 2026 volleyball season started, I had kind of written off the possibility of Marquette hanging a banner for a Big East regular season title. That’s what you do when head coach Tom Mendoza was going to have to lean heavily on a transfer and several freshmen just to get to the NCAA tournament AND Creighton started the year at #13 in the country. When the Bluejays downed preseason #9 Purdue back in August, it definitely felt like this just wasn’t going to be Marquette’s year, and that’s fine, not all of them have to be bolts out of the blue (and gold). And then Marquette grew together as a team, and they overcame long term absences from both Keira Schmidt and Emma Parks from the lineup. At the same time, Creighton hit a massive stumble in the middle of the season, losing not just to Marquette at home to break bunches of different winning streaks, but falling to Georgetown for the first time ever. That lands us with both the Golden Eagles and the Bluejays going into the final two matches of the regular season — Seton Hall & St. John’s for MU, Georgetown & Villanova for CU, both teams at home — with each at 12-2. It doesn’t matter what Creighton does in their contests, as long as Marquette wins their two matches, they’ll be Big East regular season champions for the first time under Tom Mendoza. If Creighton stumbles while Marquette wins, Marquette will be the #1 seed in the conference tournament and outright Big East champion for the first time since 2013. Just take care of business — and stay on track for that NCAA tournament at-large bid! — and hang a banner when the season is over. That’s a hell of an accomplishment just to get to this point for Mendoza and his charges, and now they get the chance, the opportunity — coaches love talking about opportunities, right? — to go out and do something that seemed wildly unlikely three months ago.
